question: Does Noisy Nodes plus Pair Update Norm retain a material 100K gain over a same-machine GPTrans-T control and transfer as frozen weights to the 500K development cohort?

hypothesis.observed_deficiency: The accepted 100K joint gain of 0.009382 eV shrank to 0.002056 eV at matched 500K, but platform, development cohort and training horizon changed together.
alternative_explanations: The 100K gain is specific to the 100K development cohort.
A longer optimization horizon lets the unregularized reference catch up.
Single-seed noise or EMA selection contributes to the apparent gain.
hypothesis.changed_mechanism: Reuse the existing joint regularizer with no architectural or hyperparameter modification, paired to a local reference.
hypothesis.cheapest_falsifier: One same-machine seed-42 60-epoch run, paired 50K development predictions and training curves; frozen-weight transfer only after both arms finish.
hypothesis.decision_changed_if_positive: Attribute the 100K gain more confidently to the regularizer under this single-seed contract, then inspect cohort transfer without a full-run promotion claim.
hypothesis.decision_changed_if_negative: Treat the historic 100K gain as cross-run or cohort-sensitive and do not budget new 500K training on it.
historical_unknowns: The exact cause of 500K gain contraction remains unisolated.

next_allowed_actions: One local RTX 5060 joint-candidate training attempt under the frozen 100K contract.

comparison_blockers: No terminal same-machine paired endpoint yet.
